data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.spec_note: mass/power fields are taken from the first sentence in the NASA description that states a mass in kg or a power in W; they may describe a sub-unit or a mode. Read the sentence.
record.name: Mars Science Entry Descent and Landing Instrument (MEDLI)
record.description: The Mars Science Laboratory Entry, Descent, and Landing Instrument (MEDLI) suite is an engineering experiment in the MSL heatshield. It is designed to measure atmospheric conditions and performance of the heatshield during entry. MEDLI comprises seven MEDLI Integrated Sensor Plugs (MISP) and seven Mars Entry Atmospheric Data System (MEADS) pressure sensors. Sensor support electronics are mounted inside the heatshield to provide power, signal conditioning, and analog-to-digital conversion. Each MISP consists of four type-K thermocouples embedded at different depths in the heatshield, nominally 0.1, 0.2, 0.45, and 0.7 inches below the surface to measure the temperatures within the heatshield as a function of time, and a single hollow aerothermal ablation and temperature sensor, which measures the propagation of the 700 degree C isotherm through the heatshield. The isotherm measurement also provides an assessment of the loss of material from the heatshield during entry. The MEDLI suite provides a detailed time history of the performance of the heatshield material. For more detailed information, see: http://msl-scicorner.jpl.nasa.gov/Instruments/MEDLI/
